title: Little bit of my AI slop journey - tech demo almost done - would you play this?
author: LegendaryJohnny
selftext:
So I am spending last 2 months most of my spare time doing this. I want to showcase that if you do not one shot your game or make game using just Claude for doing everything with its code, including models, its NOT THE SAME as spending A LOT OF TIME creating your vision.

Note - this video is just tech demo, which is not even finished. I am just implementing game logic and game mechanics all the time, so there is a lot of placeholders, almost no sounds and animations are very placeholdery without polishing.

But I acomplished following things - character creation, stats distribution, perks distribution and beginning of the game, where you can see crate looting with randomized items in - every gameplay will differ slightly and there is MANY builds to be make.

Then I accomplished the are transition to the ground, where you start inside abandonded church, if you go from abandoned church outside, there is smooth transitiont to the open world. 2 lurking NPCs around church for testing gameplay mechanics - Speech skill check - you can see it in action. Pickpocketing - inspired by Kingdom Come - its basically 1 to 1 copy of KCD minigame, not sure what rules they have in background, my rules for being successful and having more time might vastly differ. Then I implemented sneaky attack and one thing I am proud off - sneaking in grenade to NPCs pocket - you can see result, including gore limb dismemberment mechanic in the video.

Later you can hear my music - Claude created tool (I posted here the video of the tool before), I created the music you can hear in that tool.

Than you can see fights - gore mechanics again, and while zoomed in you can see rag doll and physics effects on dead bodies. Then you can see daytime change into night on one sign post (inspired by bonfires of Dark Souls serie). Then another fight with another gore effect of arm dismemberment.

I think this is forming into being entertaining RPG if I will keep up doing it. Core is almost done, I just need lockpicking and polishing animations, adding sound, music and then building the world and quests. Whole process is very entertaining and I am doing it mostly for myself because you learn so much during the journey.

Tool used:  
  
Claude, claude, claude for everything code related - pro version for 20 dollars per month.

Blender for placeholders and graphics elements - I am never opening it, Claude again is doing all the work.

Tripo 3D - paid for PRO, first month just 9 dollars, but paid 9 dollars more for more credit. Credit is running fast and you rebuild a lot of stuff because of poor results or you pay extra for cutting merged model into parts.

Music - my own tool created by Claude.

Game engine - Godot - it surprised me. Obvious choices are always Unity or Unreal, but Claude can work extremely well with Godot because it is using normal English language and I can tell - you need to add or change anything and Claude does it very quickly. On top of that it has a lot of features which are already in my game, which I did not expect they are even available for Godot - like dynamic snow where it leave traces behind (I had it in placeholder and it looks amazing, unfortunatelly I dont have it in this video), rag doll effects and other things I didnt know this engine can support.

So what do you think? Can you imagine if team of 5 people will work on something for 3 years using Claude and other tools to speed up work? I think we will see GOTY contenders made by vibecoding within 2 or 3 years EASILY.

And would you play my game once it is polished and has questline? I can tell you that fights are feeling satisfying already.
